slides.title: Two Source Systems, One Platform
slides.subtitle: Acme's data landscape today consists of two primary sources feeding downstream analytics

items: Core transactional database for orders, inventory, and financials
Batch extracts via nightly ETL jobs
~50 tables, 200 GB total volume
Change tracking enabled for incremental loads
Customer accounts, opportunities, and pipeline data
Currently extracted via third-party tool into CSVs
~30 objects, updated throughout the day
No unified view with ERP data today

slides.title: Challenges with the Current Approach
bullets: Siloed data — no single source of truth across sales and operations
Stale data — nightly batch loads mean dashboards are always a day behind
No data quality enforcement — errors propagate into reports undetected
Manual CSV pipeline for Salesforce is fragile and hard to monitor
No lineage or governance — compliance team lacks audit trail
slides.notes: These pain points are what the medallion architecture on Databricks directly addresses.

slides.title: Acme Corp — Medallion Architecture
slides.notes: The medallion architecture gives Acme three clear layers: Bronze lands raw data as-is from SQL Server and Salesforce. Silver cleanses, conforms, and joins the two sources. Gold produces business-ready tables optimized for reporting and ML.

slides.title: Medallion Layers for Acme
slides.subtitle: Each layer serves a distinct purpose in the data lifecycle

items: Land SQL Server tables via Lakeflow Connect (CDC)
Ingest Salesforce objects via Lakeflow Connect (SaaS connector)
Preserve source schema as-is
Append load metadata (timestamp, source, batch ID)
Cleanse and deduplicate records
Apply PII masking on customer fields
Conform data types across sources
Join orders (SQL Server) with accounts (Salesforce)
Customer 360 table (unified CRM + ERP view)
Revenue analytics (pipeline-to-close metrics)
Inventory health dashboard tables
Optimized star schema for BI tools

slides.title: Acme Corp — Ingestion with Lakeflow Connect
slides.notes: Lakeflow Connect provides native connectors for both SQL Server (JDBC/CDC) and Salesforce (SaaS connector). Both pipelines are governed by Unity Catalog and run on serverless compute. This replaces Acme's current nightly batch ETL and manual CSV exports with managed, incremental ingestion.

slides.title: Acme Corp — Business Intelligence
slides.notes: Once data flows through the medallion layers into Gold tables, Acme's analysts can use Databricks SQL Warehouses for ad-hoc queries, AI/BI Dashboards for self-service reporting, and Genie for natural-language questions. Unity Catalog provides row-level security and column masking for PII compliance.

items.title: Access Control

items.title: Lineage Tracking
items.description: End-to-end lineage from SQL Server / Salesforce through Bronze → Silver → Gold

items.title: Data Quality
items.description: Expectations on Silver tables catch schema drift and null violations automatically

items.title: Audit Trail
items.description: Full audit log of who accessed what data and when — ready for compliance review

steps.title: Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–3)
steps.description: Stand up Unity Catalog, configure Lakeflow Connect for SQL Server and Salesforce, build Bronze layer with CDC pipelines

steps.title: Phase 2: Curation (Weeks 4–6)
steps.description: Build Silver layer with Declarative Pipelines, apply data quality expectations, join CRM and ERP data into conformed models

steps.title: Phase 3: Business Value (Weeks 7–9)
steps.description: Build Gold tables for Customer 360 and revenue analytics, deploy Databricks SQL dashboards, onboard analysts

slides.text: One platform. Two sources. Complete visibility from ingestion to insight.
